'''Rajnath Singh''' ({{IPA|hi|ɾɑːd͡ʒnɑːt̪ʰ sɪŋɡʱ|audio=Rajnath Singh pronounciation.ogg}}; born 10 July 1951) is an Indian politician and lecturer who is serving as the 29th [[Minister of Defence (India)|Minister of Defence]] since 2019 and as the [[Leader of the House in Lok Sabha|Deputy Leader of the House, Lok Sabha]] since 2014. He is a [[Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha|Member of Parliament]] from [[Lucknow Lok Sabha constituency|Lucknow]] since 2014. He previously served as the 25th [[Minister of Home Affairs (India)|Union Minister of Home Affairs]] in the [[first Modi ministry]] from 2014 to 2019, making him the first person born after [[Indian Independence Act 1947|Indian independence]] to hold the office.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shri Rajnath Singh|url=https://www.mod.gov.in/Shri%20Rajnath%20Singh|access-date=18 February 2021|website=Ministry of Defence|archive-date=20 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210120001310/https://www.mod.gov.in/Shri%20Rajnath%20Singh|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=23 January 2013|title=Rajnath Singh elected BJP president, vows to bring back party to power|url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/politics/national/rajnath-singh-bjp-president-vows-to-bring-back-party-to-power-7938.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702122249/https://www.indiatvnews.com/politics/national/rajnath-singh-bjp-president-vows-to-bring-back-party-to-power-7938.html|archive-date=2 July 2018|access-date=18 February 2021|website=India TV News|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Jain|first=B. M.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yv4WEAAAQBAJ|title=The Geopsychology Theory of International Relations in the 21st Century: Escaping the Ignorance Trap|date=15 February 2021|publisher=Rowman & Littlefield|isbn=978-1-4985-7360-3|pages=[https://books.google.com/books?id=yv4WEAAAQBAJ&dq=Rajnath+Singh+under+Atal+bihari+vajpayee&pg=PA86 86]|language=en}}</ref> He was [[List of presidents of the Bharatiya Janata Party|President]] of the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] from 2005 to 2009 and again from 2013 to 2014. Singh is a veteran leader of the [[BJP]] who started his career as a ''swayamsevak'' of the [[Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh]].<ref name="Meet the leaders">{{Cite news |title=Meet the men and women who will run India for the next 5 years – Ministry of utmost prowess |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/elections/lok-sabha/india/meet-the-men-and-women-who-will-run-india-for-the-next-5-years/rajnath-singh-defence-minister/slideshow/69594872.cms |website=The Economic Times |access-date=19 August 2020 |archive-date=21 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021120215/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/elections/lok-sabha/india/meet-the-men-and-women-who-will-run-india-for-the-next-5-years/rajnath-singh-defence-minister/slideshow/69594872.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

Singh previously served as the [[List of Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh|chief minister]] of [[Uttar Pradesh]] from 2000 to 2002 and a [[Union Council of Ministers|Cabinet Minister]] for Road Transport and Highways in the [[Vajpayee Government]] from 1999 to 2000 and the minister of Agriculture from 2003 to 2004. He was the President of [[Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha]] from 1988 to 1990. He was a member of the [[Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly]] from [[Haidergarh (assembly constituency)|Haidergarh constituency]] twice.<ref name=":1" /> He previously represented [[Ghaziabad Lok Sabha constituency|Ghaziabad]] in the [[Lok Sabha]] from 2009 to 2014. He was also a [[member of Rajya Sabha]] from 2002 to 2008 and from 1994 to 2001.

==Early life==
Rajnath Singh was born in Bhabhaura village of [[Chandauli district]], [[Uttar Pradesh]] to father Ram Badan Singh and mother Gujarati Devi.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kaushal |first1=Pradeep |title=Jaswant is sacked without show-cause notice, but Vasundhara could defy directive to resign |url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/-jaswant-is-sacked-without-showcause-notice-but-vasundhara-could-defy-directive-to-resign-/517003 |work=Indian Express |date=15 September 2009 |access-date=21 September 2020 |archive-date=25 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200225122658/http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/-jaswant-is-sacked-without-showcause-notice-but-vasundhara-could-defy-directive-to-resign-/517003/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Bio">{{Cite web |title=Biography – Rajnath Singh |url=https://www.rajnathsingh.in/biography/ |website=rajnathsingh.in |date=7 July 2014 |access-date=25 July 2020 |archive-date=21 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021120403/https://www.rajnathsingh.in/biography/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Singh|first=Ujjwal Kumar|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HeCGAwAAQBAJ&dq=rajnath+singh+rajput&pg=PA244|title=The State, Democracy and Anti-Terror Laws in India|date=11 January 2007|publisher=SAGE Publications India|isbn=978-81-7829-955-6|language=en|access-date=19 November 2021|archive-date=8 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230408100247/https://books.google.com/books?id=HeCGAwAAQBAJ&dq=rajnath+singh+rajput&pg=PA244|url-status=live}}</ref> He was born into a family of farmers. He received his primary education from a local school of his village and went on to secure a master's degree in physics, acquiring first division results from [[Gorakhpur University]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=10 April 2019|agency=PTI|title=Rajnath Singh's biography tracing 5 decades in politics to hit stands in May|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/rajnath-singh-biography-rajneeti-1498533-2019-04-10|work=India Today|access-date=21 August 2020|archive-date=19 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019125055/https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/rajnath-singh-biography-rajneeti-1498533-2019-04-10|url-status=live}}</ref> From childhood he was inspired by the ideology of [[Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=11 March 2011|title=Shri Rajnath Singh|url=http://censusindia.gov.in/2011-Documents/ShriRajnathSingh.pdf|access-date=14 August 2020|website=[[Government of India]]|archive-date=25 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201125225805/https://www.censusindia.gov.in/2011-Documents/ShriRajnathSingh.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> He worked as a lecturer of physics at K.B. Post-Graduate College [[Mirzapur]], [[Uttar Pradesh]].<ref name="Bio" />

== Early political career ==
=== Entry into politics ===
Singh had been associated with the [[Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh]] since 1964, at the age of 13 and remained connected with the organisation. He also became [[Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh|Shakha Karyavah]] (General Secretary) of [[Mirzapur]] in the year 1972.<ref name="Bio" /> After 2 years in the year 1974, he entered politics.<ref name="Rajnath Singh elections 2020">{{Cite news |title=Rajnath Singh: Rajnath Singh BJP from LUCKNOW in Lok Sabha Elections |website=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/rajnath-singh/candidates/candidateid-11464.cms |access-date=19 August 2020 |archive-date=10 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510190901/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/rajnath-singh/candidates/candidateid-11464.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> Between 1969 and 1971 he was the organizational secretary of the [[Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad]] (the student wing of the RSS) in [[Gorakhpur]]. He became the general secretary of the RSS's [[Mirzapur]] branch in 1972.{{Sfnm|1a1=Chintamani|1y=2019|1pp=17-18|2a1=Singh|2y=2019|2pp=1-2}} In 1974, he was appointed secretary for the Mirzapur unit of the [[Bharatiya Jana Sangh]], predecessor of [[Bharatiya Janata Party]].<ref name="profile">{{cite news|title=Profile: Rajnath Singh |publisher=[[Zee News]] |url=http://www.zeenews.com/znnew/articles.asp?rep=2&aid=264537&sid=ARC |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930185718/http://www.zeenews.com/znnew/articles.asp?rep=2&aid=264537&sid=ARC |archive-date=30 September 2007 }}</ref> In 1975, aged 24, Singh was appointed District President of the [[Jana Sangh]].

=== JP Movement and Emergency ===
In the 1970s, Singh was influenced by the [[JP Movement]] of [[Jayaprakash Narayan]]. He was also arrested in the year 1975 during the state of [[National Emergency]] for associating with [[JP Movement]] and was detained for a time period of 2 years.<ref name="Did you know?">{{Cite news|title=Did you know⁠? India's Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has a master's degree in physics⁠ — and other interesting facts about his life|url=https://www.businessinsider.in/thelife/personalities/news/rajnath-singh-profile-interesting-facts-all-you-need-to-know-about-indias-minister-of-defence/slidelist/76888231.cms|website=Business Insider|access-date=22 August 2020|archive-date=31 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200831061351/https://www.businessinsider.in/thelife/personalities/news/rajnath-singh-profile-interesting-facts-all-you-need-to-know-about-indias-minister-of-defence/slidelist/76888231.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Entry into electoral politics ===
After being released from jail, Singh joined the [[Janata Party]] founded by [[Jayprakash Narayan]] and contested legislative assembly elections from Mirzapur in 1977. He successfully fought the election and was elected as a [[Member of the Legislative Assembly (India)|Member of Legislative Assembly]] from [[Mirzapur]].<ref>{{cite news |title='Wasn't given parole to meet ailing mother, could not perform last rites: Rajnath Singh recalls Emergency |url=https://m.economictimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/wasnt-given-parole-to-meet-ailing-mother-could-not-perform-last-rites-rajnath-singh-recalls-emergency/articleshow/109222741.cms |work=The Economic Times |agency=ANI |date=12 April 2024 |access-date=5 August 2024}}</ref>

=== Rise within BJP ===
At that time he gained the popularity in [[State (polity)|state politics]] and then joined [[BJP]] in the year 1980 and was one of the initial members of the Party.{{Sfn|Chintamani|2019|p=35}} He became the State President of the BJP youth wing in 1984, the National general secretary in 1986 and the National President in 1988. He was also elected into the [[Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council]].<ref name="profile" />

== Early ministerial roles ==

=== Education Minister (1991–1992) ===
In 1991, when the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] formed its first government in Uttar Pradesh under chief minister [[Kalyan Singh]], he was appointed education minister of Uttar Pradesh. He held the education portfolio for a tenure of two years.<ref name="DDMod" /> Major highlights of his tenure as education minister included the controversial [[Anti-Copying Act, 1992]], which made copying a non-bailable offence,<ref name="rediff1">{{Cite web|last=Phadnis|first=Aditi|title=How Rajnath Singh rose through the ranks|url=https://www.rediff.com/news/report/how-rajnath-singh-rose-through-the-ranks/20130131.htm|access-date=17 February 2021|website=Rediff|language=en|archive-date=2 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302055743/https://www.rediff.com/news/report/how-rajnath-singh-rose-through-the-ranks/20130131.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> modernising science texts, and incorporating [[Indian mathematics#Vedic period|vedic mathematics]] into the [[curriculum]].<ref name=":1">{{cite news |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/who-is-rajnath-singh-152326-2013-01-22 |title=Who is Rajnath Singh? |work=India Today |date=23 January 2013 |access-date=28 January 2013 |archive-date=10 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810072147/http://indiatoday.intoday.in/story/who-is-rajnath-singh/1/247240.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Anti-Copying Act, 1992 ====
{{Main|Anti-Copying Act, 1992}}

Singh helped push the controversial Anti-Copying Act in response to perceived widespread cheating in schools and colleges in Uttar Pradesh.<ref name="Did you know?" /><ref name="MassCopy">{{Cite news|date=27 February 2017|title=PM Modi brings 'mass copying' issue into political discourse|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/lucknow/pm-modi-brings-mass-copying-issue-into-political-discourse/story-dEKFZuqO5sDpa9ZAxEHzZM.html|website=Hindustan Times|access-date=21 August 2020|archive-date=20 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120130457/https://www.hindustantimes.com/lucknow/pm-modi-brings-mass-copying-issue-into-political-discourse/story-dEKFZuqO5sDpa9ZAxEHzZM.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=UP Govt to challenge order against Anti-copying Act|url=https://www.rediff.com/news/2001/feb/07up1.htm|website=rediff.com|access-date=21 August 2020|archive-date=17 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017001734/http://www.rediff.com/news/2001/feb/07up1.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> when [[Mulayam Singh Yadav]] became the [[chief minister of Uttar Pradesh]], heading [[Bahujan Samaj Party]] in the year 1993 he repealed the Act.<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 June 1994 |author=D. Gidwani |title=Mulayam Singh Yadav abolishes Anti-Copying Act in Uttar Pradesh |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/indiascope/story/19940630-mulayam-singh-yadav-abolishes-anti-copying-act-in-uttar-pradesh-809307-1994-06-30 |website=India Today |access-date=21 August 2020 |archive-date=11 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111144216/https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/indiascope/story/19940630-mulayam-singh-yadav-abolishes-anti-copying-act-in-uttar-pradesh-809307-1994-06-30 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=How students 'copying' in exams became an issue for the BJP in the early 90s |url=https://www.thenewsminute.com/article/how-students-copying-exams-became-issue-bjp-early-90s-25481 |work=The News Minute |date=23 March 2015 |access-date=9 August 2022 |archive-date=9 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809161052/https://www.thenewsminute.com/article/how-students-copying-exams-became-issue-bjp-early-90s-25481 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Modernising the education system ====
In 1991, Singh led a partial rewrite of history textbooks used in government schools and introduced [[vedic mathematics]] into the curriculum.<ref name=":1" /> Seen as loyal to the [[Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh|RSS]], a [[Hindu nationalist]] organisation, Singh's changes to state education policy were widely perceived to have been motivated by his RSS affiliation and ideological kinship with the organisation's leadership.{{Sfn|Singh|2019|p=2}} As minister, he also focused on promoting the usage of Indian languages instead of English in courses and instruction. At the same time, he stated his appreciation for knowledge of modern languages.<ref name=":13">{{Cite news|title=Need to change present education system: Home Minister Rajnath Singh|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/need-to-change-present-education-system-home-minister-rajnath-singh/articleshow/45004996.cms?from=mdr|access-date=26 August 2020|archive-date=8 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230408101748/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/need-to-change-present-education-system-home-minister-rajnath-singh/articleshow/45004996.cms?from=mdr|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Union Transport Minister (1999–2000) ===
In April 1994, he was elected into the [[Rajya Sabha]] (Upper House of the [[Parliament of India|Parliament]]) and became involved with the Advisory Committee on Industry (1994–96), Consultative Committee for the Ministry of Agriculture, Business Advisory Committee, House Committee and the Committee on Human Resource Development.<ref>{{Cite web|date=9 July 2014|title=Rajnath Singh - from 'Physics lecturer' to 'Union Home Minister'|url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/politics/national/rajnath-singh-home-minister-of-india-bjp-modi-government-latest-18798.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702150650/https://www.indiatvnews.com/politics/national/rajnath-singh-home-minister-of-india-bjp-modi-government-latest-18798.html|archive-date=2 July 2018|access-date=18 February 2021|website=www.indiatvnews.com|language=en}}</ref> On 25 March 1997, he became the President of the BJP's Uttar Pradesh unit and in 1999 became the Union Cabinet Minister for Surface Transport.<ref name="profile" />

== Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh (2000–02) ==
{{See also|Rajnath Singh ministry}}
In 2000, he became [[List of Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh|chief minister]] of Uttar Pradesh and was twice elected as MLA from [[Haidergarh (Vidhan Sabha constituency)|Haidergarh]] in 2001 and 2002.<ref name="rediff1" /> He was preceded by [[Ram Prakash Gupta]] and succeeded by [[Mayawati]] after 56 days of [[President's rule]].<ref>[[List of chief ministers of Uttar Pradesh]]</ref> He was also the last chief minister of Undivided U.P. Contributing to his appointment as state minister were his prior experience as education minister and his [[grassroots]] support from his involvement in the anti-corruption [[JP Movement]] in the 1970s.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Gupta|first=Moushumi Das|date=8 June 2019|title=Modi's one move showed Rajnath Singh's 44 years of politics can become ineffective in a day|url=https://theprint.in/opinion/newsmaker-of-the-week/modis-one-move-showed-rajnath-singhs-44-years-of-politics-can-become-ineffective-in-a-day/247444/|work=ThePrint|access-date=22 August news|title=New Defence Minister: Rajnath Singh to be the new Defence Minister, Naik to be MoS|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/rajnath-singh-to-be-the-new-defence-minister-of-india/articleshow/69593474.cms|access-date=22 August 2020|archive-date=27 November Rajnath Singh Appointed Cabinet Minister Again|url=https://www.ndtv.com/people/bjps-rajnath-singh-a-man-with-no-enemies-appointed-cabinet-minister-again-2045616|website=NDTV.com|access-date=22 August also popular among [[Rajput]]s (Thakur), a significant community in the state,<ref>{{Cite news|date=19 March 2017|title=Modi accepts MLAs' choice Yogi Adityanath as U.P. CM|url=https://www.sundayguardianlive.com/news/8799-modi-accepts-mlas-choice-yogi-adityanath-cm|website=The Sunday Guardian Live|access-date=22 August 2020|archive-date=24 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024202202/https://www.sundayguardianlive.com/news/8799-modi-accepts-mlas-choice-yogi-adityanath-cm|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=The Deep Caste Symbolism In Yogi Adityanath's Appointment As Uttar Pradesh CM|url=https://www.outlookindia.com/national/deep-caste-symbolism-in-yogi-adityanaths-appointment-as-uttar-pradesh-cm-news-298257|website=Outlook India|access-date=22 August 2020|archive-date=23 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023050026/https://www.outlookindia.com/website/story/deep-caste-symbolism-in-yogi-adityanaths-appointment-as-uttar-pradesh-cm/298257|url-status=live}}</ref> like [[Bhairon Singh Shekhawat]]. Even unlike, [[L. K. Advani]] and [[Kalyan Singh]], he was not a leader of ''Firebrand Hindutva'' ideology and was a very soft-spoken person.<ref>{{Cite web|date=18 January 2021|title=Yogi Adityanath a better Uttar Pradesh CM than I was: Rajnath Singh|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/yogi-a-better-cm-than-i-was-rajnath/articleshow/80319708.cms|access-date=17 February 2021|website=The Times of India|language=en|archive-date=3 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203154000/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/yogi-a-better-cm-than-i-was-rajnath/articleshow/80319708.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Notable reforms as chief minister ===
As chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, he accused the [[Samajwadi Party]] of favouring certain communities for jobs. Singh had said that discrimination in job opportunities should end in the state.<ref>{{Cite news|date=16 March 2017|title=3 big reforms Rajnath Singh is capable of bringing in Uttar Pradesh if he's appointed the CM|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/elections/uttar-pradesh-assembly-elections-2017/3-big-reforms-rajnath-singh-is-capable-of-bringing-in-uttar-pradesh-if-hes-appointed-the-cm/590287/|website=The Financial Express|access-date=21 August 2020|archive-date=24 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024111002/https://www.financialexpress.com/elections/uttar-pradesh-assembly-elections-2017/3-big-reforms-rajnath-singh-is-capable-of-bringing-in-uttar-pradesh-if-hes-appointed-the-cm/590287/|url-status=live}}</ref> He tried to rationalise the reservation structure in government jobs by introducing the most Backward Classes among the OBC and SC, so that the reservation system could favour those at the bottom of society.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gupta|first=Moushumi Das|date=8 June 2019|title=Modi's one move showed Rajnath Singh's 44 years of politics can become ineffective in a day|url=https://theprint.in/opinion/newsmaker-of-the-week/modis-one-move-showed-rajnath-singhs-44-years-of-politics-can-become-ineffective-in-a-day/247444/|access-date=17 February 2021|website=[[ThePrint]]|language=en-US|archive-date=29 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210129061550/https://theprint.in/opinion/newsmaker-of-the-week/modis-one-move-showed-rajnath-singhs-44-years-of-politics-can-become-ineffective-in-a-day/247444/|url-status=live}}</ref>

When Singh took office as chief minister, Uttar Pradesh had the highest state crime rate in India. Singh thus made establishing law and order a key part of his policy.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Tone up law and order, Home Minister Rajnath Singh tells UP government|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/tone-up-law-and-order-home-minister-rajnath-singh-tells-up-government/articleshow/46155425.cms|access-date=21 August 2020|archive-date=8 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230408101746/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/tone-up-law-and-order-home-minister-rajnath-singh-tells-up-government/articleshow/46155425.cms|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |agency=A. N. I. Feeds |date=10 May 2018 |title=Good improvement in law and order in UP: Rajnath |url=https://www.india.com/news/agencies/good-improvement-in-law-and-order-in-up-rajnath-3045660/ |website=India.com |access-date=21 August 2020 |archive-date=26 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201026154015/https://www.india.com/news/agencies/good-improvement-in-law-and-order-in-up-rajnath-3045660/ |url-status=live }}</ref> However, after the [[2002 Gujarat riots]] a large portion of the Indian public saw the [[BJP]] as complicit in the riots, which undermined the image of Singh's party and contributed to the loss of his position.<ref>{{Cite news|last1=M|first1=Harsh|date=24 April 2019|title=One thing was distinctly rotten about 2002 Gujarat riots: use of rape as a form of terror|url=https://theprint.in/pageturner/excerpt/one-thing-was-distinctly-rotten-about-2002-gujarat-riots-use-of-rape-as-a-form-of-terror/225511/|website=ThePrint|access-date=21 August 2020|archive-date=25 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200725223238/https://theprint.in/pageturner/excerpt/one-thing-was-distinctly-rotten-about-2002-gujarat-riots-use-of-rape-as-a-form-of-terror/225511/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Why 2002 Gujarat riots still matter|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/blogs/asia/2014/05/98891.html|publisher=Al Jazeera|access-date=21 August 2020|archive-date=5 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200805191838/https://www.aljazeera.com/blogs/asia/2014/05/98891.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 7 February 2001, Singh inaugurated the [[DND Flyway]] which connects Delhi to Noida.<ref name=":5">{{cite news |title='Noida jinx' to keep Akhilesh Yadav away from PM event |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/noida-jinx-to-keep-akhilesh-yadav-away-from-pm-event/articleshow/50372875.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=29 December 2015 |access-date=18 March 2020 |archive-date=19 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319181955/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/noida-jinx-to-keep-akhilesh-yadav-away-from-pm-event/articleshow/50372875.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Resignation ===
In the year 2002, Singh resigned from the position of chief minister after a 2-year tenure because at that time, the state [[BJP]] Government held only a minority government. After his resignation, the state was under [[President's rule]] for 56 days, until the 14th Legislative Assembly appointed [[Mayawati]] to the position of chief minister for the 3rd time.<ref name="Rajnath Singh elections 2020" />

== Rise in national politics ==

=== Union Agriculture Minister (2003–04) ===
In 2003, Singh was appointed as the [[Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare|Minister of Agriculture]] and subsequently for Food Processing in the [[National Democratic Alliance (India)|NDA]] Government led by [[Atal Bihari Vajpayee]], and was faced with the difficult task of maintaining one of the most volatile areas of India's economy.<ref name=":6">{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2003/06/11/stories/2003061100100800.htm|title=Courage, Mr Rajnath Singh|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=11 June 2003|access-date=2 January 2007|archive-date=16 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180916234436/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2003/06/11/stories/2003061100100800.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> During this period he initiated a few epoch-making projects including the Kisan Call Centre and Farm Income Insurance Scheme.<ref name=":7">[http://wikimapia.org/16811689/Shri-Rajnath-Singh-MP-Loksabh-Ghaziabad-Ex-CM-Uattar-pardesh-1-30-Raj-Nagra "Shri Rajnath Singh, MP (Ghaziabad)"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029203359/http://wikimapia.org/16811689/Shri-Rajnath-Singh-MP-Loksabh-Ghaziabad-Ex-CM-Uattar-pardesh-1-30-Raj-Nagra |date=29 October 2013 }}. wikimapia.org</ref> He brought down interest rates on Agriculture loans and also established Farmer Commission and initiated Farms Income Insurance Scheme.<ref name="achieve">[http://www.rajnathsingh.in/achievements/ "Achievements"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521165627/http://www.rajnathsingh.in/achievements/ |date=21 May 2014 }}. rajnathsingh.in</ref>

=== National President of the BJP ===
==== First time (2005–2009) ====
[[File:191218-D-WA993-1773 (49238901581).jpg|thumb|Singh in Washington at a summit.|left]]
After the BJP lost power in the [[2004 Indian general election|2004 general elections]], it was forced to sit in the Opposition. After the resignation of prominent figure [[Lal Krishna Advani]] due to controversial statements over [[Muhammad Ali Jinnah]],<ref>{{Cite news|title=Rajnath Singh|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/rajnath-singh|website=India Today|access-date=22 August 2020|archive-date=29 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029111926/https://www.indiatoday.in/rajnath-singh|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the murder of strategist [[Pramod Mahajan]], Singh sought to rebuild the party by focusing on the most basic [[Hindutva]] ideologies.<ref name="instinct">{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Its-basic-instinct-for-Rajnath-Singh/articleshow/911268.cms|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106043944/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2006-12-23/india/27815843_1_rajnath-singh-uniform-civil-code-bjp-national-executive|url-status=live|archive-date=6 November 2012|title=It's basic instinct for Rajnath Singh|work=[[The Times of India]] | first1=Lopamudra|last1=Ghatak|date=23 December 2006}}</ref> He announced his position of "no compromise" in relation to the building of a [[Ram Janmabhoomi|Ram Temple]] in [[Ayodhya]] at any cost<ref name="instinct" /> and commended the rule of Vajpayee as Prime Minister, pointing towards all the developments the [[National Democratic Alliance (India)|NDA]] made for the ordinary people of India.<ref>[http://indianewsdiary.com/?p=8951 Rajnath Singh is new BJP President] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140311070147/http://indianewsdiary.com/?p=8951 |date=11 March 2014 }}. indianewsdiary.com</ref> He also criticised the role of the English language in India, claiming that most of Indian population is unable to participate in Indian economy and cultural discourse due to extreme preferences shown to English at the expense of native languages.<ref>[http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/BJP-chief-claims-English-bad-for-India-triggers-outrage/articleshow/21178996.cms "BJP chief claims English bad for India, triggers outrage."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230426153531/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/BJP-chief-claims-English-bad-for-India-triggers-outrage/articleshow/21178996.cms |date=26 April 2023 }} ''The Times of India''. 20 July 2013</ref> Singh also suspended [[Jaswant Singh]] from the party for praising Jinnah and disrespecting the policies of [[Jawaharlal Nehru]], which also led to a wave of controversies as Jaswant Singh was a very senior leader of the party.<ref name=":12">{{Cite news|title=Jaswant is sacked without show-cause notice, but Vasundhara could defy directive to resign|newspaper=Indian Express|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/-jaswant-is-sacked-without-showcause-notice-but-vasundhara-could-defy-directive-to-resign-/517003|access-date=9 August 2020|archive-date=25 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200225122658/http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/-jaswant-is-sacked-without-showcause-notice-but-vasundhara-could-defy-directive-to-resign-/517003/|url-status=live}}</ref>  Singh had held many positions for the RSS and the BJP, including serving as the [[Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh]] and the President of the BJP's [[Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha|youth wing]]. He advocated a return to a [[Hindutva]] platform. Singh resigned after the NDA lost the [[2009 Indian general election]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=23 December 2006|first=Lopamudra|last=Ghatak|title=It's basic instinct for Rajnath Singh|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Its-basic-instinct-for-Rajnath-Singh/articleshow/911268.cms|access-date=13 October 2020|website=The Times of India|archive-date=3 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201003122503/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Its-basic-instinct-for-Rajnath-Singh/articleshow/911268.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

He became the BJP National President on 31 December 2005, a post he held till 19 December 2009. In May 2009, he was elected MP from Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/Shri%20Rajnath%20Singh%20Biodata_English.pdf|title=Ministry of Home Affairs|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170606031010/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/Shri%20Rajnath%20Singh%20Biodata_English.pdf|archive-date=6 June 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> . A bold move that will brighten Rajnath Singh's chances of winning from Ghaziabad Loksabha seat, Hundreds of Muslims joined BJP under the leadership of Raja Matin Nuri held a grand sabha in muslim dominated area [[Masuri, Ghaziabad|Masoori]], [[Dasna]] programme was also attended by [[Venkaiah Naidu|Shri M. Venkaiah Naidu]] Senior BJP Leader, Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha and Shri [[Syed Shahnawaz Hussain|Shahnawaz hussain]] that time BJP Minority Morcha President. Raja Matin Nuri also said "We have joined BJP with a hope for the better future." <ref>{{Cite news |title=Hundreds of Muslim leaders join BJP |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-others/hundreds-of-muslim-leaders-join-bjp/ |work=The Indian Express |date=16 March 2009 |access-date=3 November 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Karyakartas can create history |url=https://www.bjp.org/files/kamal-sandesh-documents/ks-april-1-09-e_2.pdf |website=BJP.org |access-date=4 November 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Dhar |first=Aarti |date=19 March 2015 |title=Indian Muslims are patriots: Rajnath |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/indian-muslims-are-patriots-rajnath/article7010877.ece |work=The Hindu |issn=0971-751X |access-date=4 November 2026}}</ref> [[File:A delegation from Kerala led by the Rajya Sabha MP, Shri A.K. Antony calling on the Union Home Minister, Shri Rajnath Singh, in New Delhi on August 30, 2018.JPG|thumb|A delegation of Rajnath Singh in [[Kerala]] with former [[Ministry of Defence (India)|Ministry of Defence of India]], [[A. K. Antony]] and [[Alphons Kannanthanam]].]]

==== Second time (2013–2014) ====
On 24 January 2013, following the resignation of [[Nitin Gadkari]] due to corruption charges, Singh was re-elected as the BJP's National President.<ref>{{cite news |agency=Press Trust of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Rajnath-steps-down-Gadkari-takes-over-as-BJP-president/articleshow/5356182.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025150732/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2009-12-19/india/28067924_1_rajnath-singh-nitin-gadkari-bjp-president |url-status=live |archive-date=25 October 2012 |title=Rajnath steps down, Gadkari takes over as BJP president |date=19 December 2009 |work=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=28 January 2013}}</ref>

Singh was on record shortly after the law [[Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code]] was re-instated in 2013, claiming that his party is "unambiguously" in favour of the law, also claiming that "We will state (at an all-party meeting if it is called) that we support Section 377 because we believe that homosexuality is an unnatural act and cannot be supported."<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/1131214/jsp/nation/story_17679913.jsp |title=BJP comes out, vows to oppose homosexuality|last=Rameshan|first=Radhika|date=13 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216103934/https://www.telegraphindia.com/1131214/jsp/nation/story_17679913.jsp|archive-date=16 December 2013|website=The Telegraph}}</ref> Singh was elected president for his second term after Gadkari stepped down in 2013. Singh played a large role in the BJP's campaign for the [[2014 Indian general election]], including declaring [[Narendra Modi]] the party's Prime Ministerial candidate despite opposition from within the BJP. After the party's landslide victory, Singh resigned the party presidency to assume the position of Home Minister.<ref>{{Cite web|date=9 July 2014|title=Rajnath Singh – from 'Physics lecturer' to 'Union Home Minister'|url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/politics/national/rajnath-singh-home-minister-of-india-bjp-modi-government-latest-18798.html|access-date=13 October 2020|website=www.indiatvnews.com|archive-date=2 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702150650/https://www.indiatvnews.com/politics/national/rajnath-singh-home-minister-of-india-bjp-modi-government-latest-18798.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

He contested the 2014 Lok Sabha elections from [[Lucknow (Lok Sabha constituency)|Lucknow]] constituency and was subsequently elected as a [[Member of Parliament (India)|Member of the Parliament]].<ref name="the hindu">[http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-otherstates/rajnath-singh-surpasses-vajpayees-victory-margin-in-lucknow/article6021382.ece "Rajnath Singh surpasses Vajpayee's victory margin in Lucknow"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230411061521/https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-otherstates/rajnath-singh-surpasses-vajpayees-victory-margin-in-lucknow/article6021382.ece |date=11 April 2023 }}. ''The Hindu''. 18 May 2014</ref>

== Union Home Minister (2014–19) ==
[[File:Shri Raj Nath Singh taking charge as the Union Minister for Home Affairs, in New Delhi on May 29, 2014.jpg|alt=|thumb|Singh taking charge as the Union Minister for Home Affairs, in New Delhi on 29 May 2014.]]
[[File:Indian delegation led by the Union Home Minister, Shri Rajnath Singh holding a bilateral meeting with Russian delegation led by the Minister for Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation, Mr. Vladimir Kolokolstsev, in Moscow.jpg|thumb|248x248px|Singh holding a bilateral meeting with Russian delegation led by the Minister for Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation, Vladimir Kolokolstsev, in Moscow]]
Rajnath Singh was appointed the [[Minister of Home Affairs (India)|Union Minister of Home Affairs]] in the [[Narendra Modi]] [[First Modi ministry|government]] and was sworn in on 26 May 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/portfolios-of-the-union-council-of-ministers-2/|title=Portfolios of the Union Council of Ministers|website=pmindia.gov.in|access-date=24 December 2019|archive-date=14 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214014324/https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/portfolios-of-the-union-council-of-ministers-2/|url-status=live}}</ref> At the time he was the former president of the party and was the one who named [[Narendra Modi]] as the prime ministerial candidate for the party. After the win of the party in 2014 Lok Sabha election he took over the position from [[Sushilkumar Shinde]] as the [[Minister of Home Affairs (India)|Minister of Home Affairs]] from the year 2014–2019. He has also been the current Deputy Leader of Lok Sabha since 2019.{{Sfn|Singh|2019|p=2}}{{Citation needed|date=August 2024}}

=== JNU incident ===
Singh triggered controversy amid the protests over the police action at [[Jawaharlal Nehru University, Delhi|Jawaharlal Nehru University]] (JNU), on 14 February 2016, claiming that the "[[Jawaharlal Nehru University sedition row|JNU incident]]" was supported by [[Lashkar-e-Taiba]] chief Hafiz Saeed.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-news-india/rajnath-singh-hafiz-saeed-let-jnu-protests-had-support-of-let-chief-hafiz-saeed-rajnath-singh/|title=Understand the reality... Lashkar chief Hafiz Saeed backed JNU incident: Home Minister Rajnath Singh|date=15 February 2016|access-date=24 December 2019|archive-date=22 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190822100139/https://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-news-india/rajnath-singh-hafiz-saeed-let-jnu-protests-had-support-of-let-chief-hafiz-saeed-rajnath-singh/|url-status=live|work=The Indian Express}}</ref> He gave the statement in the backdrop of [[Anti-national (India)|anti-national]] speeches in JNU related to the hanging anniversary of Kashmiri Separist [[Maqbool Bhat]] and [[Afzal Guru]] on 9 February 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|date=11 February 2016|title=Afzal Guru: A martyr in JNU campus? Anti-India slogans raised, no arrests made|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/education-today/news/story/jnu-afzal-guru-308204-2016-02-11|access-date=13 October 2020|website=India Today|archive-date=28 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128053321/https://www.indiatoday.in/education-today/news/story/jnu-afzal-guru-308204-2016-02-11|url-status=live}}</ref> After the statement there were protests against Singh. After the arrests of [[Umar Khalid]] and [[Kanhaiya Kumar]], he met with many leaders from the left.<ref>{{Cite web|date=16 February 2016|title=JNU row: Who said what on the issue|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/fyi/story/jnu-row-rajnath-singh-kiren-rijiju-kanhaiya-kumar-309004-2016-02-16|access-date=13 October 2020|website=India Today|archive-date=6 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506012053/https://www.indiatoday.in/fyi/story/jnu-row-rajnath-singh-kiren-rijiju-kanhaiya-kumar-309004-2016-02-16|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|agency=PTI|date=13 February 2016|title=Left leaders meet Rajnath Singh over JNU issue|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/jnu-row-left-leaders-meet-rajanth-singh/article8233159.ece|access-date=13 October 2020|issn=0971-751X|archive-date=12 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200912063559/https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/jnu-row-left-leaders-meet-rajanth-singh/article8233159.ece|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Infiltration ===
In May 2016, he claimed that infiltration from Pakistan declined by 52% in a period of two years.<ref>{{Cite web|date=28 May 2016|title=Narendra Modi's 56-inch chest not reduced an inch: Rajnath Singh|url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/280516/narendra-modi-s-56-inch-chest-not-reduced-an-inch-rajnath-singh.html|access-date=17 February 2021|website=Deccan Chronicle|language=en|archive-date=4 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210304071322/https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/280516/narendra-modi-s-56-inch-chest-not-reduced-an-inch-rajnath-singh.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Bharat Ke Veer App ===
On 9 April 2017, he launched [[Bharat Ke Veer]] web portal and application with Bollywood actor [[Akshay Kumar]]. This was an initiative taken by him for the welfare of martyrs' family.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=160767|title=Shri Rajnath Singh inaugurates Web Portal 'Bharat ke Veer'|website=pib.nic.in|access-date=11 April 2017|archive-date=11 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411140014/http://pib.nic.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=160767|url-status=live|date=9 April 2017}}</ref> Bharat Ke Veer is a fund-raising initiative by the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India on behalf of members of the Indian paramilitary forces.<ref>{{Cite news|title='Bharat Ke Veer' initiative pays off, people donate generously|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/bharat-ke-veer-initiative-pays-off-people-donate-generously/articleshow/60109913.cms|access-date=21 September 2020|archive-date=2 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180802133545/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/bharat-ke-veer-initiative-pays-off-people-donate-generously/articleshow/60109913.cms|url-status=live|date=17 August 2017}}</ref> Singh himself praised the app and was its first donor.{{Sfn|Chintamani|2019|p=247}} An official anthem was launched on 20 January 2018 by him along with film star [[Akshay Kumar]], and other ministers [[Kiren Rijiju]] and [[Hansraj Gangaram Ahir|Hansraj Ahir]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/magazines/panache/akshay-kumar-rajnath-singh-unveil-official-anthem-of-bharat-ke-veer/articleshow/62581609.cms|title=Akshay Kumar, Rajnath Singh unveil official anthem of 'Bharat Ke Veer'|date=20 January 2018|access-date=14 February 2018|archive-date=15 February === Doklam matter ===
{{Main|2017 India China border standoff}}

[[File:The Urban Development Minister of Nepal, Shri Arjun Narsingh K.C. calling on the Union Home Minister, Shri Rajnath Singh, in New Delhi on December 19, 2016.jpg|thumb|Urban Development Minister of Nepal,  [[Arjun Narasingha K.C.|Arjun Narsingh K.C.]] calling on the  Singh, in New Delhi]]
[[Doklam]] is a disputed territory between [[Bhutan]] and China.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Haran |first=VP |date=5 September 2017 |title=Doklam Dispute: Part I. A Brief History |url=https://www.ipcs.org/comm_select.php?articleNo=5353 |access-date=15 September 2026 |website=Institute of Peace and Conflict Studies}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Joshi |first=Manoj |author-link=Manoj Joshi (journalist) |date=9 August 2017 |title=Doklam: To start at the very beginning |url=https://www.orfonline.org/research/doklam-start-very-beginning |access-date=15 September 2026 |website=[[Observer Research Foundation]]}}</ref> In June 2017, in this disputed territory, China attempted to construct a road.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2017 |title=Recent Developments in Doklam Area |url=https://www.mea.gov.in/press-releases?dtl/28572/Recent_Developments_in_Doklam_Area |access-date=15 September 2026 |website=Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India}}</ref> The Indian Army stepped-in on behalf of Bhutan resulting in a border standoff with the [[People's Liberation Army]] of China.<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 July 2017 |title=China says India violates 1890 agreement in border stand-off |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/world/china-says-india-violates-1890-agreement-in-border-stand-off-idUSKBN19O108/ |access-date=15 September 2026 |work=Reuters |language=en-US}}</ref> The Doklam area is also strategically important for India due to its proximity with the [[Siliguri Corridor]].<ref>{{Cite report |url=https://www.rand.org/pubs/commentary/2017/09/what-were-chinas-objectives-in-the-doklam-dispute.html |title=What Were China's Objectives in the Doklam Dispute? |last=Blank |first=Jonah |author-link=Jonah Blank |date=8 September 2017 |publisher=[[RAND Corporation]]}}</ref> As home minister, Singh co-chaired an all-party meeting related to the standoff on 15 July 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mohan |first=Geeta |date=15 July 2017 |title=India-China face-off: After all-party meet, Congress calls for lowering tension through diplomacy, to raise issue in Parliament |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/india-china-face-off-doklam-congress-parliament-sushma-swaraj-rajnath-singh-1024425-2017-07-15 |access-date=15 September 2026 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref> On 21 August 2017, speaking to the [[Indo-Tibetan Border Police]] (ITBP), Rajnath Singh stated that India wanted peace with its neghbours but was ready to fight for its territory; he also said that "There will be a solution soon and I am sure China will make a positive move."<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Solution To Doklam Standoff Will Be Found Soon, Says Rajnath Singh|url=https://www.outlookindia.com/making-a-difference/solution-to-doklam-standoff-will-be-found-soon-says-rajnath-singh-news-300589|magazine=Outlook India|access-date=9 August 2020|archive-date=24 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924014039/https://www.outlookindia.com/website/story/solution-to-doklam-standoff-will-be-found-soon-says-rajnath-singh/300589|url-status=live|date=21 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=22 August 2017 |title=China responds with propaganda to Rajnath's hope of Doklam standoff resolution |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/doklam-standoff-china-continues-with-standard-propaganda-attack/articleshow/60176350.cms |access-date=15 September 2026 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257 |agency=PTI}}</ref> The standoff ended a week later.

=== Commissioning of Bastariya Battalion ===
On 21 May 2018, he commissioned [[Bastariya Battalion]]. As Union Home Minister, Rajnath Singh attended the passing out parade of 241 Bastariya Battalion of [[Central Reserve Police Force|CRPF]] in Ambikapur, Chhattisgarh on 21 May 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/first-ever-passing-out-parade-of-bastariya-battalion-held-in-chhattisgarh-1238057-2018-05-21|title=First ever graduation parade of 'Bastariya Battalion' held in Chhattisgarh|website=India Today|access-date=6 August 2018|archive-date=6 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180806151058/https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/first-ever-passing-out-parade-of-bastariya-battalion-held-in-chhattisgarh-1238057-2018-05-21|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Union Defence Minister (2019–present)==
[[File:Shri Rajnath Singh taking charge as the Union Minister for Defence, in New Delhi on June 01, 2019.jpg|thumb|Rajnath Singh taking charge as the Union Minister for Defence, in the presence of [[Shripad Naik]], Minister of State for Defence, in New Delhi on 1 June 2019.]]
[[File:Shri Rajnath Singh assumed charge as the Union Minister of Defence for the second consecutive term, in New Delhi on June 13, 2024.jpg|thumb|Rajnath Singh takes office as the Minister of Defense of India for the second consecutive term, in New Delhi on 13 June 2024.]]
Singh became the [[Minister of Defence (India)|defence minister]] of India on 31 May 2019.<ref>{{citation |title=PM Modi allocates portfolios. Full list of new ministers |url=https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/pm-modi-allocates-portfolios-full-list-of-new-ministers-1559288502067.html |work=[[Live Mint]] |date=31 May 2019 |access-date=2 June 2019 |archive-date=2 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190602015648/https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/pm-modi-allocates-portfolios-full-list-of-new-ministers-1559288502067.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Among the challenges that the Defence Minister is expected to address are the ever-increasing requirements of India's forces, including increased budgetary requirements, especially in the light of an unstable neighbourhood.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news|title=Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh In His 2.0 Avatar|url=http://businessworld.in/article/Union-Defence-Minister-Rajnath-Singh-In-His-2-0-Avatar/19-09-2019-176397|website=[[Businessworld|BW Businessworld]]|access-date=20 August 2020|archive-date=5 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191005032002/http://www.businessworld.in/article/Union-Defence-Minister-Rajnath-Singh-In-His-2-0-Avatar/19-09-2019-176397/|url-status=live|last=Jha|first=Suman K.|date=19 September 2019}}</ref> As Union Defence Minister, Singh has indicated a subtle shift in India's strategic vision; this includes a focus on decreasing the import of [[weapon]]s and making the nation an arms exporter with an [[arms industry]].<ref name=":11">{{Cite web|title=India to emerge as major defence exporter: Rajnath Singh|url=https://government.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/india-to-emerge-as-major-defence-exporter-rajnath-singh/73117819|access-date=20 August 2020|website=ETGovernment.com|archive-date=22 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022160602/https://government.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/india-to-emerge-as-major-defence-exporter-rajnath-singh/73117819|url-status=live}}</ref> He has supported various reforms including those for greater representiation of women in the defence services.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Rajnath Singh: Latest News & Videos, Photos about Rajnath Singh |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/Rajnath-Singh |website=The Economic Times |access-date=20 August 2020 |archive-date=14 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200814063937/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/Rajnath-Singh |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Trivedi |first=Saurabh |date=4 August 2025 |title=Defence panel reviews women's role; Rajnath vows greater representation |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/defence-panel-reviews-womens-role-rajnath-vows-greater-representation/article69893505.ece |url-access=subscription |access-date=14 September 2026 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=17 February 2020 |title=Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh wholeheartedly welcomes Supreme Court's judgement on Permanent Commission for women in Army |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1603488&reg=48&lang=2 |access-date=14 September 2026 |website=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref>
[[File:PM dedicates to the nation HAL Helicopter Factory at Tumakuru, Karnataka on February 06, 2023.jpg|thumb|Singh, along with Prime Minister Modi inaugurates Asia's largest helicopter manufacturing sector ([[Hindustan Aeronautics Limited|HAL]]) at [[Tumkur]], in [[Karnataka]] in 2023.]]

=== Rafale fighter plane ===
{{Main|Rafale deal}}

[[File:The Union Minister for Defence, Shri Rajnath Singh with the French Minister of Armed Forces, Ms. Florence Parly, in France on October 08, 2019.jpg|thumb|254x254px|Singh with the French Minister of Armed Forces, [[Florence Parly]]]]
[[Dassault Rafale]] is a fighter plane of French origin whose deal was signed by then [[Minister of Defence (India)|Minister of Defence]], [[Manohar Parrikar]], in 2016 to increase the strength of the [[Indian Air Force]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=P |first1=Rajat |date=1 February 2012 |title=French jet Rafale bags $20bn IAF fighter order; India 'briefs' losing European countries |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/French-jet-Rafale-bags-20bn-IAF-fighter-order-India-briefs-losing-European-countries/articleshow/11706551.cms |website=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=10 August 2020 |archive-date=12 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112024901/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/French-jet-Rafale-bags-20bn-IAF-fighter-order-India-briefs-losing-European-countries/articleshow/11706551.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[Government of India]] had signed to buy 126 fighter jets costing $30 billion.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Sagar|first=Pradip R.|date=26 January 2014|title=dna exclusive: 100% price escalation on Rafale fighter aircraft to Rs 1.75 lakh crore likely to dent IAF's strike capability|url=https://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-dna-exclusive-100-price-escalation-on-rafale-fighter-aircraft-to-rs-175-lakh-crore-likely-to-dent-iaf-s-strike-capability-1957107|website=[[DNA India]]|access-date=10 August 2020|archive-date=12 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201012221224/https://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-dna-exclusive-100-price-escalation-on-rafale-fighter-aircraft-to-rs-175-lakh-crore-likely-to-dent-iaf-s-strike-capability-1957107|url-status=live}}</ref>

The planes were received during Rajnath Singh's tenure as the defence minister. Though a controversial issue, Singh completed the deal after becoming defence minister; the Indian Air Force received its first Dassault Rafale on 8 October 2019 and he personally went to France to receive it.<ref name=":9">{{Cite news|date=8 October 2019|title=Rajnath Singh receives first Rafale in France; delivery in May 2020|work=[[The Hindu]]|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/india-receives-first-rafale-fighter-jet-from-france/article29618964.ece|issn=0971-751X|access-date=10 August 2020|archive-date=9 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809171657/https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/india-receives-first-rafale-fighter-jet-from-france/article29618964.ece|url-status=live}}</ref> The first fleet of 5 fighter jets landed at [[Ambala Air Force Station]] in July 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Philip|first=Snehesh Alex|date=29 July 2020|title=India's Rafale lands in Ambala, Rajnath warns those who threaten territorial integrity|url=https://theprint.in/defence/indias-rafale-lands-in-ambala-rajnath-warns-those-who-threaten-territorial-integrity/470446/|website=[[ThePrint]]|access-date=10 August 2020|archive-date=5 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200805110541/https://theprint.in/defence/indias-rafale-lands-in-ambala-rajnath-warns-those-who-threaten-territorial-integrity/470446/|url-status=live}}</ref> Singh said that "Those wanting to threaten India's territorial integrity should be worried about its new capability."<ref>{{Cite news|date=29 July 2020|title=Welcoming Rafale, Rajnath gives a veiled warning to China|url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/while-welcoming-rafale-rajnath-gives-a-veiled-warning-to-china-11596024182626.html|website=[[Livemint]]|access-date=10 August 2020|archive-date=19 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220519123828/https://www.livemint.com/news/india/while-welcoming-rafale-rajnath-gives-a-veiled-warning-to-china-11596024182626.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The further procurement of 26 more Rafales (22 single-seater and 4 double-seater) for the Indian Navy was signed on 28 April 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=India and France sign Intergovernmental Agreement on 26 Rafale Jets for Indian Navy |url=https://in.ambafrance.org/India-and-France-sign-Intergovernmental-Agreement-on-26-Rafale-Jets-for-Indian |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250502225133/https://in.ambafrance.org/India-and-France-sign-Intergovernmental-Agreement-on-26-Rafale-Jets-for-Indian |archive-date=2 May 2025 |access-date=31 May 2025 |website=La France en Inde / France in India |language=en |url-status=live |date=28 April 2025}}</ref>

Singh said that talks must continue and status quo must be restored.<ref name=":15" /><ref name=":16" /> Throughout the tensions, multiple talks took place at multiple levels.<ref>{{Cite web |website=India Today}}</ref>

[[File:SCO Defense Ministers meeting (2023).jpg|thumb|327x327px|Singh at the [[Shanghai Cooperation Organisation|SCO]] defence ministers' meeting in New Delhi on 28 April 2023]]
On 28 April 2023, Chinese Defense Minister [[Li Shangfu]] met with Rajnath Singh as part of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation defence ministers' meeting in New Delhi, making it the first visit to India by a Chinese Defence Minister since the 2020 border skirmishes.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-65399808 |title=SCO: China defence minister in India amid border tensions |access-date=4 June 2023 |newspaper=BBC |date=28 April 2023 |archive-date=25 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240125085613/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-65399808 |url-status=live }}</ref> Disengagement was completed by December 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 December 2024 |title=Statement by External Affairs Minister, Dr. S. Jaishankar in Lok Sabha |url=https://www.mea.gov.in/speeches-statements?dtl/38665/Statement_by_External_Affairs_Minister_Dr_S_Jaishankar_in_Lok_Sabha |access-date=23 September 2026 |website=Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India}}</ref>

On 26 June 2025, Singh visited China to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation defence ministers' meeting in Qingdao, marking the first visit by a senior Indian minister to China since the 2020 border skirmishes and the first by an Indian Defence Minister in 12 years. During the meeting, Singh refused to sign the joint declaration, citing the document's failure to condemn the [[2025 Pahalgam attack]] in [[Kashmir]], which claimed 26 lives, and lack of alignment with India's stance against terrorism.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.firstpost.com/india/rajnaths-china-visit-for-sco-marks-new-phase-in-india-china-thaw-since-modi-xi-2024-meet-13900508.html|title=Rajnath's China visit for SCO marks new phase in India–China thaw since Modi-Xi 2024 meet|newspaper=Firstpost|first=Shreya|last=Mundhra|date=25 June 2025|access-date=27 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/rajnath-singh-refuses-to-sign-sco-document-that-removed-pahalgam-and-had-balochistan-8764415|title=India Refuses To Sign SCO Document That Skipped Pahalgam, Had Balochistan|newspaper=NDTV|first=Shiv|last=Aroor|date=26 June 2025|access-date=27 June 2025|author-link=Shiv Aroor}}</ref>

===Russia===
{{See also|India and the Russian invasion of Ukraine}}Rajnath Singh has on multiple occasions supported dialogue and diplomacy as a way towards easing tensions stemming from the [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]].<ref name=":17">{{Cite web |date=24 August 2022 |title=SCO member states must fight together & eliminate terrorism in all its forms: Raksha Mantri during Defence Ministers' meet in Uzbekistan |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1854128&reg=48&lang=2 |access-date=24 September 2026 |website=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref><ref name=":18">{{Cite web |date=26 October 2022 |title=Telephonic conversation between Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh & Defence Minister of Russia Mr Sergei Shoigu |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1870962&reg=48&lang=2 |access-date=24 September 2026 |website=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref> He has expressed concern about the humanitarian situation and nuclear posturing.<ref name=":17" /><ref name=":18" />

International military exercises known as [[Vostok 2022]] were launched in Russia's Far East in September 2022, with countries including Russia, India and China taking part in it.<ref>{{cite news |title=Explainers Explained: What does India's participation in Russia's military drills Vostok-2022 mean? |url=https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/explained-what-does-indias-participation-in-russias-military-drills-vostok-2022-mean-11167031.html |work=Firstpost |date=2 September 2022 |access-date=3 June 2023 |archive-date=28 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528235350/https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/explained-what-does-indias-participation-in-russias-military-drills-vostok-2022-mean-11167031.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 28 April 2023, Singh met with Russian Minister of Defence [[Sergei Shoigu]].<ref>{{cite news |title=India, Russia agree to boost longstanding defence ties |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/india-russia-reiterate-commitment-towards-defence-partnership-govt-statement-2023-04-28/ |work=Reuters |date=28 April 2023 |access-date=3 June 2023 |archive-date=3 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603214051/https://www.reuters.com/world/india-russia-reiterate-commitment-towards-defence-partnership-govt-statement-2023-04-28/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 10 December 2024, Singh held talks with Russian Defence Minister [[Andrey Belousov]]. Singh reaffirmed India's commitment to strengthening defence ties with Russia.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Peri |first1=Dinakar |date=10 December 2024 |title=Despite pressure, India consciously decided to deepen engagement with Russia: Rajnath Singh |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/despite-pressure-india-consciously-decided-to-deepen-engagement-with-russia-rajnath/article68970362.ece |work=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=24 December 2024}}</ref>

In a lecture in 2025, as a takeaway from the war, the defence minister stated "In the Ukraine-Russia conflict, drones have virtually emerged as a new arm, if not a transformative science."<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 April 2025 |title=Armed Forces must operate jointly & remain future-ready in today's ever-evolving multi-domain environment: Raksha Mantri at DSSC, Wellington |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2120678&reg=3&lang=2 |access-date=24 September 2026 |website=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref> In 2026, again with reference to the war and drones he stated, "From the drone's molds to its software, engines, and batteries, everything must be manufactured in India."<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 March 2026 |title=India must become global hub of drone manufacturing in next few years amid current geopolitical instability: Raksha Mantri at National Defence Industries Conclave 2026 |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2242398&reg=48&lang=2 |access-date=24 September 2026 |website=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref>[[File:Defence Minister of Bharat Shri Rajnath Singh with President of The Russian Federation Mr. Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin.jpg|thumb|Singh with Russian President [[Vladimir Putin]] in Moscow on 10 December 2024]]

=== Agnipath Scheme ===
{{Main|Agnipath Scheme}}

The [[Ministry of Defence (India)|Defence Ministry]] introduced a "transformative" military recruitment scheme called [[Agnipath Scheme|Agnipath]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last= |date=16 June 2022 |title=Explained {{!}} The Agnipath scheme for armed forces |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/agnipath-scheme-eligibility-recruitment-salary-benefits-soldiers-army-navy-air-force/article65529801.ece |access-date=16 September 2026 |work=The Hindu |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> The recruitment was pursued for all the three forces, and the selected 46,000 candidates were termed as "''Agniveers''".<ref name=":2" /> The scheme faced opposition and various protests were held.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 June 2022 |title=Agnipath: India strike over controversial army hiring plan |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-61836637 |access-date=16 September 2026 |website=BBC}}</ref> Railway property was set on fire and losses were suffered in [[Bihar]], [[Telangana]] and [[West Bengal]];<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=23 June 2022 |title=Agnipath protests: Railways suffer losses over Rs 1,000 crore, highest in a decade |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/agnipath-protests-indian-railways-suffer-damages-thousand-crore-1965950-2022-06-23 |magazine=India Today |access-date=5 August 2022 |archive-date=5 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220805161814/https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/agnipath-protests-indian-railways-suffer-damages-thousand-crore-1965950-2022-06-23 |url-status=live }}</ref> the opposition also called it an [[Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh|RSS]] agenda.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=23 June 2022 |title=Agnipath an RSS agenda: HDK |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/karnataka/2022/Jun/23/agnipath-an-rss-agenda-hdk-2468681.html |access-date=16 September 2026 |website=The New Indian Express}}</ref> The Ministry said it was a long pending reform in the defence field to lower the average age of the military.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Agnipath protests Highlights: Agnipath a long-pending reform, govt concessions pre-planned, says Defence Ministry |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/agnipath-protests-live-updates-indian-army-7976434/ |access-date=5 August 2022 |work=The Indian Express |date=18 June 2022 |archive-date=5 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220805161814/https://indianexpress.com/article/india/agnipath-protests-live-updates-indian-army-7976434/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[Delhi High Court]] stated that it finds no reason to interfere in the process and that the government has brought in the scheme "in national interest".<ref>{{Cite news |date=28 February 2023 |title='In national interest': HC upholds Agnipath validity |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/in-national-interest-hc-upholds-agnipath-validity/articleshow/98286708.cms |access-date=1 March 2023 |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=28 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228102920/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/in-national-interest-hc-upholds-agnipath-validity/articleshow/98286708.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> Singh has called the scheme "successful".<ref>{{Cite news |date=26 May 2024 |editor-last=Achom |editor-first=Debanish |title=Exclusive: Rajnath Singh's 'Back Off' Reply To Opposition On Playing Politics Over Agnipath Scheme |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/exclusive-rajnath-singhs-back-off-reply-to-opposition-on-playing-politics-over-agnipath-scheme-5748197 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260418192146/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/exclusive-rajnath-singhs-back-off-reply-to-opposition-on-playing-politics-over-agnipath-scheme-5748197 |archive-date=18 April 2026 |access-date=16 September 2026 |work=NDTV}}</ref>

=== 2025 India-Pakistan Conflict ===
{{Main|2025 India–Pakistan conflict|2025 India–Pakistan crisis|l2 = crises}}

The [[India–Pakistan conflict (2025)|India-Pakistan conflict in 2025]] took place between 7–10 May.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clary |first=Christopher |date=28 May 2025 |title=Four Days in May: The India-Pakistan Crisis of 2025 • Stimson Center |url=https://www.stimson.org/2025/four-days-in-may-the-india-pakistan-crisis-of-2025/ |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=[[Stimson Center]]}}</ref> On 7 May 2025, Rajnath Singh said that India had utilized its "right to respond" by attacking terror infrastructure with "precision, precaution and compassion";<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=7 May 2025 |title=India used its 'right to respond,' says Rajnath Singh on Op Sindoor; lauds Army for 'scripting history' |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/india/2025/May/07/india-used-its-right-to-respond-says-rajnath-singh-on-op-sindoor-lauds-army-for-scripting-history |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=[[The New Indian Express]] |agency=[[Press Trust of India|PTI]]}}</ref> Singh was addressing the Raising Day event of Border Roads Organisation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 May 2025 |title=Through Operation Sindoor, India used its 'Right to Respond' to the attack on its soil: Raksha Mantri |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2127561&lang=2&reg=48 |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref> He stated, "we have followed the ideals of [[Lord Hanuman]]. Just as he said during the destruction of [[Ashoka Vatika|Ashok Vatika]] — 'I only struck those who attacked me' — we too have targeted only those who killed our innocent people."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chopra |first=Ritika |date=8 May 2025 |title=Rajnath flags precision of Operation Sindoor strikes: Have only struck those who killed innocents |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/hanuman-ashok-vatika-defence-minister-rajnath-singh-response-sindoor-9988709/ |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=[[The Indian Express]]}}</ref> The next day, at the National Quality Conclave, Singh said that "[[Operation Sindoor]] was successfully executed because our formidable and professionally-trained armed forces were equipped with high-quality equipment."<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 May 2025 |title=Operation Sindoor was successfully executed because our formidable & professionally-trained Armed Forces were equipped with high-quality equipment, says Raksha Mantri at National Quality Conclave 2025 |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2127735&reg=48&lang=2 |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref> On 11 May, at the inauguration of a [[BrahMos]] centre, Singh said that "Operation Sindoor was not just a military action, but a symbol of India's political, social and strategic willpower."<ref name=":19">{{Cite web |date=11 May 2025 |title=Operation Sindoor not just a military action, but a symbol of India's political, social & strategic willpower: Raksha Mantri |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2128133&lang=2&reg=48 |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref> He connected it to India's earlier responses to terrorism, the [[2016 Indian Line of Control strike]] following the [[2016 Uri attack|Uri attack]], and the [[2019 Balakot airstrike]] following the [[2019 Pulwama attack|Pulwama attack]].<ref name=":19" /> On 16 May, at [[Bhuj Air Force Station]], he said that "India’s fight against terrorism is not just a matter of security, it has now become a part of the national defence doctrine, and we will root out this hybrid and proxy warfare". He said Operation Sindoor was not over and could restart.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 May 2025 |title=India's fight against terrorism is now part of national defence doctrine, we will root out this hybrid & proxy warfare: Raksha Mantri at Bhuj Air Force Station |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2129052&reg=48&lang=2 |access-date=27 September 2026 |website=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref> On 20 June, while interacting with soldiers in [[Udhampur]], he reiterated, "Operation Sindoor is not over yet. This is just a pause. I want to tell this to my neighbouring country."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Khajuria |first=Sanjay |date=21 June 2025 |title='Operation Sindoor' is proof new India will respond to terror with strength & strategy: Rajnath Singh |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/operation-sindoor-is-proof-new-india-will-respond-to-terror-with-strength-strategy-rajnath-singh/articleshow/121982566.cms |access-date=27 September 2026 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

In July 2025, Rajnath Singh, addressing the [[Indian parliament]], rejected US President [[Donald Trump]]'s claim that the United States had mediated the ceasefire between India and Pakistan in May, stating that India had not acted under any external pressure. Singh clarified that military operations, launched in response to the [[2025 Pahalgam attack]], ceased only after all political and military objectives were achieved. He further stated that the decision to halt "Operation Sindoor" followed a request from Pakistan's Director General of Military Operations, who sought relief from continued hostilities.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 July 2025 |title=India says no foreign pressure to stop conflict with Pakistan |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5y204pmrp2o |access-date=29 July 2025 |website=BBC |last=Sebastian|first=Meryl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=28 July 2025 |title=Defence minister denies India bowed to pressure to end fighting with Pakistan |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/defence-minister-denies-india-bowed-pressure-end-fighting-with-pakistan-2025-07-28/ |access-date=29 July 2025 |work=Reuters |language=en|last=Dayal|first=Sakshi}}</ref> Trump has taken credit for the ceasefire on over 40 different occasions.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=26 August 2025 |title=Trump repeats claim of brokering India-Pakistan ceasefire with 100% tariff threat |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/world/us-news/story/donald-trump-repeats-claim-brokering-india-pak-ceasefire-100-tariff-threat-glbs-2776696-2025-08-26 |access-date=26 September 2026 |website=India Today |agency=[[Press Trust of India]]}}</ref>

In November 2025, he said that "tomorrow [[Sindh]] may return to India again."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Trivedi |first1=Saurabh |title=Sindh will always be a part of India's civilisational heritage, says Rajnath |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/sindh-may-return-to-india-someday-says-rajnath-singh/article70314994.ece |website=The Hindu |access-date=24 November 2025 |date=23 November 2025|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Murad, Sherry slam Indian defence minister's remarks on Sindh |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1957175 |website=Dawn |access-date=25 November 2025 |date=25 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Momand |first1=Abdullah |last2=Syed |first2=Baqir Sajjad |title=FO denounces Indian defence minister's 'delusional, dangerously revisionist' remarks about Sindh |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1956894 |website=Dawn |date=23 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hindu Council denounces India's Sindh claim |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2579651/hindu-council-denounces-indias-sindh-claim |website=The Express Tribune |access-date=29 November 2025 |date=29 November 2025}}</ref>

=== RAKSHA ===
On 3 September 2026, Singh released RAKSHA, a ten year framework for defence diplomacy.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=3 September 2026 |title=Rajnath Singh sets 10-year push for defence diplomacy under new RAKSHA plan |url=http://defence.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/policy-partnerships/rajnath-singh-sets-10-year-push-for-defence-diplomacy-under-new-raksha-plan/133732308 |access-date=24 September 2026 |website=ETDefence.com}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He married Savitri Singh on 5 June 1971, with whom he has two sons and a daughter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Members : Lok Sabha |url=http://164.100.47.194/Loksabha/Members/MemberBioprofile.aspx?mpsno=4268 |website=164.100.47.194 |access-date=18 August 2020 |archive-date=27 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027033519/http://164.100.47.194/Loksabha/Members/MemberBioprofile.aspx?mpsno=4268 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="DDMod">{{cite web|url=https://ddpmod.gov.in/sites/default/files/RMprofile6619.pdf|title=Shri Rajnath Singh Hon'ble Raksha Mantri|access-date=18 August 2020|archive-date=22 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022020340/https://www.ddpmod.gov.in/sites/default/files/RMprofile6619.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> His son [[Pankaj Singh (politician)|Pankaj Singh]] is a politician and [[Member of the Legislative Assembly (India)|Member of the Legislative Assembly]] from [[Noida (Assembly constituency)|Noida]], [[Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly|Uttar Pradesh]] from BJP.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Shukla|first=Ankita|date=17 November 2018|title=राजनाथ सिंह जीवनी, इतिहास, जाति, शिक्षा, परिवार, पत्नी, माता, पिता !!|url=https://oyehero.com/political/rajnath-singh-biography-in-hindi/|website=Oye Hero|access-date=25 July 2020|archive-date=25 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200725112620/https://oyehero.com/political/rajnath-singh-biography-in-hindi/|url-status=live}}</ref> Singh is a devout [[Hindu]] and a religious man and is known for soft-spoken behaviour.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lakshmi|first=Rama|date=12 October 2019|title=With Rafale puja, Rajnath Singh was just Hindu Everyman. Criticising him is political suicide|url=https://theprint.in/opinion/with-rafale-puja-rajnath-singh-was-just-hindu-everyman-criticising-him-is-political-suicide/304628/|access-date=5 May 2021|website=[[ThePrint]]|language=en-US|archive-date=1 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201201175458/https://theprint.in/opinion/with-rafale-puja-rajnath-singh-was-just-hindu-everyman-criticising-him-is-political-suicide/304628/|url-status=live}}</ref>
